sop_modules.name: Porch Floor Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Crew mobilization and equipment staging, clear furniture/planters/obstacles from porch or patio surface. Ground-level work — no ladder or scaffold staging required.

tasks.name: Crew Mobilization & Equipment Staging
tasks.description: Mobilize crew, transport coating materials, rollers, brushes, sprayer (if spray_backroll), diamond grinder or acid etch supplies (concrete), and anti-slip aggregate to job site. Stage equipment in protected area adjacent to work surface.

quality_notes.all: Verify all coating system materials match TDS requirements. Confirm anti-slip aggregate type matches spec (silica sand for field, aluminum oxide for steps). Stage materials in shade to prevent premature heating.

tasks.name: Clear Porch/Patio Surface
tasks.description: Remove all furniture, planters, grills, doormats, and other obstacles from porch or patio surface. Stage items in adjacent covered area or garage. Document pre-existing surface condition (cracks, stains, prior coatings).

quality_notes.all: Photograph surface condition before clearing. Note any existing cracks, spalling, or coating failure for prep planning. Confirm owner approval if heavy items (hot tub, built-in planters) cannot be moved.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Mobilize first -> Clear surface area second. Surface must be fully accessible before protection deployment.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor Perimeter Protection
sop_modules.description: Tape and mask all surfaces adjacent to porch floor: wall-floor junction, railing post bases, door thresholds, landscape edges, and hardscape transitions. Protection scope depends on porch geometry and adjacent features.

tasks.name: Wall-Floor Junction Masking
tasks.description: Apply masking tape and paper at wall-to-floor junction along full perimeter where wall meets porch floor. 3-6 inches of paper up wall face to catch roller splatter and coating creep. Use exterior-grade masking tape rated for 7+ day adhesion.

quality_notes.all: Tape must be pressed tight to floor surface to prevent coating wicking under edge. Use 6-inch paper minimum — wider for spray_backroll method.

tasks.name: Railing Post Base Masking
tasks.description: Tape and mask railing post bases where posts meet porch floor surface. Wrap tape around post base perimeter and apply paper collar to prevent coating contact with railing finish. Conditional — only when railings are present.

quality_notes.all: Wrap tape fully around each post base. Ensure no gaps where coating can creep behind tape onto railing finish.

tasks.name: Door Threshold Masking
tasks.description: Mask door thresholds at porch-to-interior transitions. Apply tape along threshold edge and paper/plastic over threshold surface. Prevent coating from contacting threshold metal or wood. Count per door.

quality_notes.all: Critical masking point — threshold is high-visibility. Tape must be crisp and tight. Extend paper 6 inches past threshold onto interior floor if door will remain open during application.

tasks.name: Landscape Edge Protection
tasks.description: Deploy drop cloth along porch/patio perimeter where landscape beds are adjacent. Protect plantings from coating splash, acid etch runoff (concrete prep), and pressure wash debris. Conditional — only when landscape is adjacent.

quality_notes.all: Extra coverage needed during acid etch phase — acid runoff damages vegetation. Extend plastic 3-4 ft from porch edge.

tasks.name: Hardscape Edge Protection
tasks.description: Tape and drop cloth at hardscape transitions (driveway, sidewalk, adjacent patio sections not being coated). Prevent coating overspray and acid etch contact. Conditional — only when adjacent hardscape exists.

quality_notes.all: Tape at the transition line to create clean edge. Canvas drop cloth for traffic areas.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Wall base first -> Railing bases -> Door thresholds -> Landscape edge -> Hardscape edge. Work from structure outward.

sop_modules.name: Concrete Moisture Testing
sop_modules.description: Perform MVER (calcium chloride) and/or relative humidity (RH) testing on concrete substrate. MANDATORY hard stop for all concrete porch and patio coatings. MVER > 5 lbs/1000 SF/24hr or RH > 85% requires moisture-mitigating primer before any coating. Test locations: minimum 1 per 500 SF, 3 minimum for any project.

tasks.name: MVER / RH Moisture Testing
tasks.description: Perform moisture vapor emission rate (MVER) testing using calcium chloride method (ASTM F1869) and/or relative humidity testing using in-situ probes (ASTM F2170). Minimum 3 test locations per project, 1 additional per 500 SF over 1500 SF. Allow 60-72 hours for MVER test results. HARD STOP: MVER > 5 lbs/1000 SF/24hr OR RH > 85% = do NOT proceed with standard primer — must use moisture-mitigating primer system.

hard_stop.description: Excessive moisture vapor emission. Standard coatings will delaminate. Must apply moisture-mitigating primer (TSK_PRFL_PRIME_MOISTURE_MITIGATING) before any topcoat system.

quality_notes.all: Document all test locations and results. Photograph each test setup and result. Results become permanent project record. Do not proceed to prime or apply without documented passing results OR moisture-mitigating primer specification.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Moisture test must complete and pass BEFORE any prep profiling begins. Results drive primer selection.

sop_modules.name: Concrete Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Concrete-specific prep: surface profiling (acid etch for CSP 1, diamond grind for CSP 2-3), crack filling, and final cleaning. Profile method is driven by coating_system — penetrating stains need light profile (CSP 1), film-forming coatings need mechanical profile (CSP 2-3). All tasks conditional on substrate_type = concrete.

tasks.name: Acid Etch Surface Profile (CSP 1)
tasks.description: Apply phosphoric or muriatic acid solution to concrete surface per ICRI CSP-1 (light profile). Spread acid, scrub with stiff broom, neutralize with baking soda solution, rinse thoroughly. Achieves sandpaper-like texture for penetrating products. Required for concrete_stain and acrylic_sealer coating systems.

quality_notes.all: Verify CSP-1 profile achieved with ICRI comparator chips. Surface should feel like medium sandpaper. Neutralize fully — residual acid destroys coating adhesion. Rinse until pH neutral (test with pH strips). Allow 24-48 hr dry before coating.

tasks.name: Diamond Grind Surface Profile (CSP 2-3)
tasks.description: Mechanically grind concrete surface using diamond-segment floor grinder to achieve ICRI CSP 2-3 profile. Required for film-forming coatings (porch_enamel, polyurea) that need mechanical bond. More aggressive than acid etch. Generates significant dust — connect vacuum/dust collection.

quality_notes.all: Verify CSP 2-3 with ICRI comparator chips. Surface should show open pores and feel rough. Remove all grinding slurry. Edge areas not reachable by floor grinder must be hand-ground with angle grinder + diamond cup wheel.

tasks.name: Crack Fill with Patching Compound
tasks.description: Fill cracks, spalls, and divots in concrete surface with appropriate patching compound. Hairline cracks (<1/8 in): use crack filler. Medium cracks (1/8-1/4 in): use polymer-modified patching compound. Large cracks (>1/4 in): use hydraulic cement or epoxy crack filler. Structural cracks = stop work and consult engineer.

quality_notes.all: Chase cracks with grinder before filling for better bond. Feather patch edges flush with surface. Allow patch to cure per manufacturer TDS before coating (typically 24 hr). Overfill slightly and sand flush after cure.

tasks.name: Final Clean After Profiling
tasks.description: Remove all dust, debris, grinding slurry, and acid residue from concrete surface after profiling. Vacuum with HEPA vacuum, then damp mop. Surface must be completely clean and dry before primer or coating application. Final contamination check with water drop test (water should absorb, not bead).

quality_notes.all: Water drop test: apply water drops to profiled surface — should absorb within 30 seconds. If water beads, profile is insufficient or contaminant remains. Re-clean or re-profile as needed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Profile (acid etch OR diamond grind, never both) -> Crack fill -> Final clean. Profiling method determined by coating_system. Clean must be last step before primer.

sop_modules.name: Wood Porch Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Wood-specific prep: mill glaze removal (new milled lumber), moisture content verification, adhesion sanding, and final cleaning. All tasks conditional on substrate_type = wood. Wood porch floors are typically tongue-and-groove or deck-board construction.

tasks.name: Mill Glaze Removal
tasks.description: Remove mill glaze from new milled lumber surfaces using chemical mill glaze remover or mechanical sanding with 60-80 grit. Mill glaze is a burnished surface layer created during milling that prevents coating adhesion. Common on new tongue-and-groove porch flooring.

quality_notes.all: Water drop test after treatment: water should absorb into wood within 10 seconds. If water beads, mill glaze is still present — repeat treatment. Chemical remover preferred for tongue-and-groove (reaches into gaps).

tasks.name: Wood Moisture Content Verification
tasks.description: Verify wood moisture content using pin-type or pinless moisture meter. Test minimum 5 locations across porch floor surface. HARD STOP: MC > 15% = do not coat. Wood must equilibrate to ambient conditions before coating. Re-test after 24-48 hours if initial test fails.

hard_stop.description: Wood moisture content exceeds 15%. Coating over wet wood causes adhesion failure, blistering, and peeling. Allow wood to dry and re-test.

quality_notes.all: Document all test locations and readings. Test shaded areas and areas near downspouts separately — these dry slower. Record ambient temperature and humidity at time of testing.

tasks.name: Adhesion Profile Sanding
tasks.description: Light sand entire wood porch floor surface with 80-100 grit to create adhesion profile for coating. Use random orbital sander for field areas, hand sand at edges and tongue-and-groove joints. Sand with grain direction only.

quality_notes.all: Sand with grain only — cross-grain scratches show through coating. 80 grit for softwoods (pine, fir), 100 grit for hardwoods (mahogany, ipe). Do not over-sand — goal is adhesion profile, not material removal.

tasks.name: Dust & Clean After Sanding
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from wood surface and tongue-and-groove joints. Vacuum with brush attachment, then tack cloth entire surface. Blow out T&G joints with compressed air if available. Surface must be dust-free before primer application.

quality_notes.all: Run hand over surface — should feel smooth with no grit. Check T&G joints for trapped dust. Dust in joints prevents primer penetration and causes adhesion failure at board edges.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Mill glaze removal (if new wood) -> Moisture test (hard stop) -> Adhesion sanding -> Final clean. Moisture test must pass before proceeding to sand.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Apply appropriate primer based on substrate_type and coating_system. Concrete: alkali-resistant masonry primer (porch_enamel), polyurea manufacturer basecoat, or moisture-mitigating primer (contingency). Wood: exterior wood primer. Self-priming systems (acrylic_sealer) and penetrating systems (concrete_stain) skip this module entirely.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Masonry Primer — Roll
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant masonry primer to profiled concrete surface by roller. Use 3/8-inch nap roller cover for smooth concrete, 1/2-inch for broom finish. Work primer into surface pores with moderate roller pressure. Apply at manufacturer-specified spread rate.

quality_notes.all: Maintain wet edge. Work in 4-ft wide strips. Back-roll each pass to ensure full pore penetration. Check coverage — primer should fully seal surface with no exposed concrete visible after drying. Cut in at wall base and railing bases with brush before rolling field.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Masonry Primer — Spray + Backroll
tasks.description: Spray alkali-resistant masonry primer onto profiled concrete surface, immediately followed by backroll with 3/8-1/2 inch nap roller to force primer into surface pores. Two-person operation: one sprays, one follows with roller. Spray-only is PROHIBITED on concrete — backroll is mandatory for pore penetration.

quality_notes.all: Spray pattern: 50% overlap passes. Backroll within 2 minutes of spray — do not let primer skin over before backrolling. Crew of 2 MINIMUM for spray_backroll. Spray-only without backroll is PROHIBITED on concrete surfaces.

tasks.name: Wood Porch Primer — Roll
tasks.description: Apply exterior wood primer to sanded wood porch floor by roller. Use 3/8-inch nap roller cover. Work primer into wood grain and T&G joint edges. Primer provides adhesion base and tannin blocking for porch enamel topcoat.

quality_notes.all: Roll with grain direction. Ensure primer penetrates into T&G joints — use brush to work primer into gaps. Full coverage, no holidays. Allow full dry time per TDS before topcoat.

tasks.name: Wood Porch Primer — Brush Edges & T&G Gaps
tasks.description: Brush primer into tongue-and-groove gaps, board edges, and perimeter cut-in areas that roller cannot reach. Use 3-inch brush to work primer into joints and against wall base masking. Companion task to TSK_PRFL_PRIME_WOOD_ROLL.

quality_notes.all: Work primer into every T&G joint and board gap. Unprimed joint edges are the primary failure point for porch floor coatings — moisture enters through uncoated end grain and causes peeling.

tasks.name: Polyurea Manufacturer Basecoat
tasks.description: Apply polyurea system manufacturer-specified basecoat/primer to diamond-ground concrete surface. Product is system-specific — must use exact manufacturer primer paired with polyurea topcoat. Typically a two-component product requiring on-site mixing. Short pot life (15-30 min typical).

quality_notes.all: Follow manufacturer mix ratios EXACTLY. Mix only what can be applied within pot life. Do not thin or modify. Apply within recoat window specified by TDS. Temperature must be within manufacturer range (typically 50-90 F).

tasks.name: Moisture-Mitigating Primer (Contingency)
tasks.description: Apply moisture-mitigating primer to concrete surface that failed MVER/RH testing. Epoxy-based moisture barrier that reduces vapor emission to acceptable levels for topcoat adhesion. Typically two-component, 12-24 hour cure. This is a CONTINGENCY task — only activated when TSK_PRFL_MOISTURE_TEST hard stop triggers.

quality_notes.all: Two-component product — follow mix ratios exactly. Apply at specified spread rate with no holidays. Use spike roller to release air bubbles. Allow full cure (12-24 hr typical) before topcoat. Re-test MVER after cure to confirm reduction.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Concrete primer tasks (1-2, 5-6) and wood primer tasks (3-4) are mutually exclusive — only one substrate branch activates. Moisture-mitigating primer (6) is contingency only. acrylic_sealer and concrete_stain coating systems skip this module entirely.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor Coating Application
sop_modules.description: Apply finish coating to porch floor surface. Task selection driven by coating_system dimension: porch_enamel (concrete or wood), acrylic_sealer (concrete only, self-priming), concrete_stain (concrete only, penetrating + requires sealer topcoat), polyurea (concrete only, over manufacturer basecoat). Step detail task activates when has_steps = true.

tasks.name: Porch Enamel — Roll Field
tasks.description: Roll porch and floor enamel on field area using 3/8-inch nap roller. Apply in 4-ft wide strips maintaining wet edge. Work toward exit to avoid stepping on wet coating. Two coats required — allow full dry between coats per TDS (typically 4-6 hours). Applicable to both concrete and wood substrates.

quality_notes.all: Plan exit path BEFORE starting — cannot walk on wet coating. Maintain wet edge to avoid lap marks. Two coats minimum. Check DFT with wet film gauge on first coat.

tasks.name: Porch Enamel — Brush Edges & Detail
tasks.description: Brush porch enamel at wall base edges, railing post bases, T&G joints (wood), and other areas roller cannot reach. Cut in before rolling field. Use 3-inch brush for straight edges, 2-inch for detail work.

quality_notes.all: Cut in 3-4 inches from edges. Feather brush marks into field area so roller blends over them. On wood, work enamel into T&G joints thoroughly.

tasks.name: Porch Enamel — Spray + Backroll
tasks.description: Spray porch enamel onto floor surface, immediately followed by backroll with 3/8-inch nap roller. Two-person crew: sprayer + roller operator. Spray-only is PROHIBITED on floor surfaces — backroll ensures even film build and eliminates texture inconsistency. For large porch/patio areas (>200 SF).

quality_notes.all: Backroll within 2 minutes of spray application. Spray-only WITHOUT backroll is PROHIBITED. Two coats required. Plan work direction toward exit.

tasks.name: Acrylic Sealer — Roll (Concrete Only)
tasks.description: Roll acrylic sealer on acid-etched concrete surface. Acrylic sealer is a self-priming, film-forming clear or tinted coating. Apply in thin, even coats — typically two coats. Do not over-apply (causes whitening/blushing). Concrete substrate only.

quality_notes.all: Thin coats only — heavy application causes whitening (blushing). Two coats, allow 2-4 hours between coats. Do not apply if rain expected within 24 hours. Temperature 50-90 F. Self-priming — no separate primer required.

tasks.name: Concrete Stain Application (Concrete Only)
tasks.description: Apply concrete stain (acid-based reactive or water-based penetrating) to acid-etched concrete surface. Stain is a penetrating product — it does not form a film. Apply by sprayer, roller, or brush per manufacturer TDS. Multiple coats may be needed for desired color intensity. Concrete substrate only. REQUIRES separate clear topcoat sealer after curing.

quality_notes.all: Acid stain: apply in random circular pattern for natural appearance. Water-based stain: apply in even strokes. Do NOT allow puddles. Clean neutralization residue (acid stain) before sealer topcoat. Stain alone provides NO wear protection — topcoat sealer is MANDATORY.

tasks.name: Polyurea Topcoat — Roll (Concrete Only)
tasks.description: Apply polyurea topcoat system to manufacturer-primed concrete surface. Two-component product requiring on-site mixing. Short pot life (20-45 min typical). Roll in thin, even coats. Single coat typical but verify with manufacturer TDS. Concrete substrate only.

quality_notes.all: Mix only what can be applied within pot life. Do not thin or modify. Maintain consistent film build — thin spots will wear through first. Temperature must be within manufacturer range. Anti-slip aggregate must be broadcast into wet polyurea within working time.

tasks.name: Step Tread Coating — Edge Detail
tasks.description: Apply coating to step treads and risers with detail brush and small roller. Steps require careful edge work at nosing and riser-to-tread junction. Coating must wrap around step nosing. Count per step (tread + riser = 1 EA). Activated when has_steps = true.

quality_notes.all: Wrap coating around step nosing — exposed nosing edges are highest wear point. Coat every other step to allow passage (alternating step pattern), then return for remaining steps after dry. Verify anti-slip aggregate coverage on step treads.

tasks.name: Clear Acrylic Topcoat Over Concrete Stain
tasks.description: Apply clear acrylic topcoat sealer over cured concrete stain. MANDATORY — concrete stain is penetrating and provides NO wear protection or UV resistance on its own. Topcoat sealer protects stain color and provides abrasion resistance. Apply 2 coats minimum. Allow stain to cure per manufacturer TDS before sealing (typically 24 hr for acid stain after neutralization, 4-6 hr for water-based).

quality_notes.all: Thin coats — heavy application causes blushing/whitening. Two coats minimum for wear resistance. Allow 2-4 hours between coats. This sealer topcoat is what receives the anti-slip aggregate broadcast (on final coat).

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Only ONE coating system branch activates per project. Porch enamel tasks (1-3): brush edges -> roll OR spray_backroll field. Acrylic sealer (4): roll only. Concrete stain (5) -> cure -> sealer topcoat (8). Polyurea (6): roll over manufacturer basecoat. Step detail (7) activates with any coating system when has_steps = true.

sop_modules.name: Anti-Slip Aggregate Broadcast
sop_modules.description: Broadcast anti-slip aggregate into wet final coat. MANDATORY for ALL exterior floor coating systems — safety requirement. Silica sand for field areas, aluminum oxide for step treads (higher durability at wear points). Aggregate is broadcast while final coat is still wet, then excess is swept after cure.

tasks.name: Anti-Slip Broadcast — Floor Field
tasks.description: Broadcast silica sand (40-60 mesh) evenly into wet final coat on porch floor field area. Apply at approximately 1 lb per 40-60 SF. Broadcast within 5-10 minutes of coating application while surface is still tacky. After cure, lightly sweep to remove loose excess aggregate. MANDATORY for all exterior floor coatings.

quality_notes.all: Even distribution is critical — clumps create rough spots, bare areas are slip hazards. Broadcast by hand for small areas, use hand-crank spreader for >100 SF. Timing is critical: too early = aggregate sinks below surface, too late = aggregate does not embed.

tasks.name: Anti-Slip Broadcast — Step Treads
tasks.description: Broadcast aluminum oxide aggregate into wet final coat on step treads. Aluminum oxide is harder and more durable than silica sand — required at high-wear step nosings. Apply by hand, focusing on nosing area and full tread face. MANDATORY when has_steps = true.

quality_notes.all: Concentrate aggregate at step nosing where foot traffic is heaviest. Even coverage across full tread face. Aluminum oxide is preferred over silica sand for steps due to superior hardness and wear resistance.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Field broadcast (1) during field coating application. Step broadcast (2) during step coating application. Both must occur while final coat is wet — coordinate timing with apply module.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor Cleanup & Demobilization
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection masking, return furniture and items to porch, perform final inspection and touch-up, clean tools and dispose of waste materials. Final inspection includes slip resistance verification.

tasks.name: Remove All Protection Masking
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, paper, plastic sheeting, and drop cloths from wall bases, railing bases, door thresholds, landscape edges, and hardscape edges. Pull tape at 45-degree angle while coating is firm but not fully cured for cleanest edge. Dispose of contaminated materials properly.

quality_notes.all: Pull tape at 45 degrees toward the coated surface. If coating has fully cured and is bridging tape, score with utility knife before pulling to prevent edge peeling. Inspect all previously masked surfaces for coating bleed-through.

tasks.name: Return Furniture & Items to Porch
tasks.description: Move staged furniture, planters, and accessories back to porch surface. Use felt pads under furniture legs to protect new coating from scratches. Do NOT return heavy items until coating has achieved full cure (typically 72 hours for porch enamel, 7 days for full hardness).

quality_notes.all: Light foot traffic OK after 24 hours for most coatings. Heavy furniture 72+ hours. Full cure/hardness at 7 days — advise homeowner. Place felt pads under ALL furniture legs to prevent indentation and scratching of new coating.

tasks.name: Final Inspection & Touch-Up
tasks.description: Walk entire porch floor surface inspecting for holidays, thin spots, lap marks, drips, and edge quality. Verify anti-slip aggregate coverage is uniform. Touch up any defects with brush. Test slip resistance by walking surface in work boots — coating should feel gritty/textured, not smooth.

quality_notes.all: Check: (1) No holidays or missed spots, (2) Even color and sheen, (3) Clean edges at wall base and railing bases, (4) Anti-slip aggregate evenly distributed, (5) No drips or runs on step risers, (6) Slip resistance confirmed by walk test.

tasks.name: Tool Cleanup & Demobilization
tasks.description: Clean all tools, roller covers, brushes, spray equipment. Dispose of acid etch waste, grinding dust, and contaminated drop cloths per local regulations. Pack and load equipment. Demobilize from job site.

quality_notes.all: Acid etch waste must be neutralized before disposal. Do not pour acid residue into storm drains. Grinding dust from concrete contains silica — dispose per local hazmat guidelines. Leave work area clean and debris-free.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Remove protection -> Replace furniture -> Final inspection -> Tool cleanup & demobilize. Furniture replacement may be deferred to follow-up visit if coating needs extended cure time.

key_porch_floor_rules_enforced: Anti-slip aggregate is MANDATORY for ALL exterior floor coating systems — broadcast into wet final coat.
Spray on concrete = ALWAYS spray_backroll (spray-only PROHIBITED). Backroll forces coating into pores.
Moisture test (MVER/RH) is MANDATORY hard stop for concrete substrates before any coating.
Concrete stain requires separate clear acrylic topcoat sealer — stain alone has NO wear protection.
Concrete surface profiling method driven by coating_system: acid etch (CSP 1) for penetrating, diamond grind (CSP 2-3) for film-forming.
Wood moisture content must be <=15% (hard stop).
acrylic_sealer is self-priming — skips prime module entirely.
concrete_stain is penetrating — no primer, no surface film, requires topcoat sealer.
Polyurea uses manufacturer-specific basecoat/primer — not interchangeable.
Step treads use aluminum oxide anti-slip (harder than silica sand) due to high-wear.
Plan exit path before applying — cannot walk on wet floor coating.

assumptions.value: Spray on concrete porch floor = auto-add backroll. Spray-only is PROHIBITED on porous concrete.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §6: Spray bridges over pinholes/voids; back-rolling forces coating into pores.
assumptions.note: Parallel to masonry spray_backroll requirement. Concrete porch floors have same porous substrate characteristics as masonry walls.

assumptions.value: Anti-slip aggregate broadcast is mandatory for ALL exterior floor coating systems — no exceptions.
assumptions.source: Building code safety requirements; industry standard practice for exterior horizontal coated surfaces.
assumptions.note: No specific doctrine for anti-slip on porch floors. This is a universal safety requirement for coated exterior walking surfaces. Silica sand for field, aluminum oxide for steps.

assumptions.value: Concrete stain is penetrating only — provides color but NO wear protection. Clear acrylic topcoat sealer is MANDATORY.
assumptions.note: Without topcoat sealer, concrete stain will wear off rapidly under foot traffic and UV exposure. Topcoat also receives the anti-slip aggregate.

assumptions.value: MVER/RH moisture testing applies to CONCRETE substrates only. Wood uses pin-type MC meter (different test).
assumptions.source: ASTM F1869 (MVER) and ASTM F2170 (RH) apply to concrete substrates. Wood MC per ASTM D4442.
assumptions.note: Concrete moisture vapor emission is a different phenomenon than wood moisture content. Different tests, different thresholds, different remediation.

assumptions.value: Acid etch (CSP 1) for penetrating products (stain, sealer). Diamond grind (CSP 2-3) for film-forming products (enamel, polyurea).
assumptions.source: ICRI Technical Guideline No. 310.2: Selecting and Specifying Concrete Surface Preparation for Sealers, Coatings, Polymer Overlays, and Concrete Repair.
assumptions.note: CSP selection is a function of coating type, not quality tier. Penetrating products need minimal profile; film-forming products need aggressive mechanical profile for adhesion.

assumptions.value: Acrylic sealer systems are self-priming — no separate primer coat needed on properly profiled concrete.
assumptions.source: Manufacturer TDS for concrete acrylic sealers; Exterior_Concrete_Masonry_Floors_Doctrine.md.
assumptions.note: Acrylic sealers penetrate into concrete profile and form their own adhesion bond. Adding primer under acrylic sealer can cause inter-coat delamination.

assumptions.value: Polyurea systems require manufacturer-specific basecoat — generic primers are NOT acceptable.
assumptions.source: Polyurea system manufacturer TDS; industry practice for multi-component floor coating systems.
assumptions.note: Polyurea chemistry requires specific basecoat for cross-linking bond. Generic alkali-resistant primer will NOT provide adequate adhesion for polyurea topcoat. Must specify manufacturer system as complete package.

assumptions.value: Epoxy floor coatings are EXCLUDED from v1. Epoxy requires separate spec due to different surface prep (shot blasting), multi-component mixing, and narrow environmental windows.
assumptions.source: Research decision — complexity scoping for v1.
assumptions.note: Epoxy porch/garage floor coatings have fundamentally different workflow (shot blasting, 2-part mixing, temperature-critical pot life, flake broadcasting, clear topcoat). Warrants separate spec family.

exclusions.reason: Epoxy requires shot blasting (not acid etch or diamond grind), 2-component mixing with strict pot life, vinyl chip broadcasting, and clear epoxy topcoat. Fundamentally different workflow. Separate spec family needed.

Garage floors have different substrate conditions (oil stains, tire marks, hot tire pickup), different prep requirements (degreasing, oil contamination testing), and typically use epoxy systems excluded from v1.
Interior concrete floors (basement, laundry room) have different moisture dynamics, no anti-slip requirement, and different product selections. Separate spec family.
exclusions.source: Domain boundary — this spec is exterior only

exclusions.reason: Stamped concrete has different profiling requirements (cannot diamond grind pattern) and uses specific clear sealers only. Separate spec or variant needed.

concrete_stain.note: Penetrating stain + mandatory clear topcoat sealer
